source.title: Softmax Gradient Tampering: Decoupling the Backward Pass for Improved Fitting
source.authors: Bishshoy Das; M. Mondal; B. Lall; S. Joshi; Sumantra Dutta Roy

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary section, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training accuracy for a CIFAR-10 model and compares it with a modified-gradient recipe; this bears on training fit but does not test most conditions in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ImageNet results and CIFAR-10 grid-search findings. ImageNet accuracy and filter-norm plots are not rows for the claim versions. The CIFAR-10 statement is about training accuracy; the grid-search values appear only in figures and are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The supplementary CIFAR-10 experiment reports saturated training accuracy for a convolutional network, directly bearing on V1 using the same training-classification measure. The main PGT comparisons do not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that PGT generally improves ImageNet fitting and predictive accuracy and can accelerate training, while reducing degenerate filter behavior in non-normalized networks. They report no benefit on CIFAR-10 because training accuracy is already saturated.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies PowerGrad Transform, which modifies gradients at the softmax layer. It does not test the original claim's recipe or its random-label conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset size: the authors say PGT has no effect on small datasets such as CIFAR-10 because networks almost always achieve 100% training accuracy. On ImageNet, reported accuracy changes vary by model, batch size, scheduler, and α.

fits_no_version.finding: PGT improves ImageNet training and test accuracies and matches the ResNet-50 baseline test accuracy in 60 rather than 100 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Modifying softmax backward gradients can improve fitting and accelerate attainment of a target accuracy on ImageNet.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.2 reports unsuccessful training of non-normalized ResNet-34 and ResNet-50 and filter zeroing in non-normalized ResNet-18.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the tested recipes, residual shortcuts alone do not ensure successful training without batch normalization as depth increases.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 passage gives no exact baseline measurement, and the cited grid-search results are figure-only. The paper's main tabulated experiments use ImageNet-1K, not CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100.
record.rows_left_out: ImageNet-1K accuracy comparisons in Tables 1–3 do not measure the CIFAR training-error behavior named by the versions. Filter-norm and feature-norm plots in Figures 5–7 and supplementary Figures 14–17 concern zeroing-out, not training classification error. CIFAR-10 grid-search points in Figure 13 are figure-only and not separately described numerically.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, explicit random-initialization checks, size dependence, early stopping, and comparisons across regularized recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-local-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized networks and matched identity-shortcut comparisons; special tanh initialization and Fixup.
Initialization comparisons, signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to measured stability thresholds, curvature trajectories, recovery, and divergence.
Matched batch-normalization comparisons of training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: ImageNet endpoint accuracies do not test V1's CIFAR-specific claim. Non-normalized residual-network failures do not test V3's plain batch-normalized comparison, and endpoint BN/non-BN differences alone do not establish V6's speed or learning-rate claims.

versions.untested_parts: Tests only the stated CIFAR-10 training-accuracy outcome for ResNet-20; does not report CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller-model comparisons, early stopping, or the claimed range of recipes.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.operation_detail: Training on CIFAR-10; the passage describes the baseline training outcome and says PGT has no effect because training accuracy is already saturated.

conditions.value: baseline; figure caption identifies grid search over PGT α

rows.value: networks almost always achieve 100% training accuracy
rows.locator: Supplementary section 8.2, Figure 13 and accompanying text
rows.note: The text attributes the lack of PGT effect on small datasets to networks almost always achieving 100% training accuracy. It does not give a separate numeric baseline value for ResNet-20.
rows.check: The value is a qualitative statement accompanying the ResNet-20 grid search, not a separately reported baseline measurement. The 360-epoch budget applies to the grid-search points; the text does not identify which runs attained 100% or specify their initialization.

relationships.reason: R1 reports that training accuracy almost always reaches 100%, consistent with near-zero training classification error; individual run values are not supplied.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
